teaser: A small country should not race for GPUs: the opportunity is the plumbing its talent stands on, built once as open infrastructure, with small models.
core_idea: For a small country such as Portugal, Romania or Estonia the race for frontier models, GPUs and data centres is a commoditised layer only capital can win, and the opportunity is at the other end of the map: the plumbing a talented person needs to sell a service to the world, forming a company, hiring across a border, being paid across Europe, working in every language, contracts and tax, which is still custom built in most of Europe and should be infrastructure the state builds once, open source and on open schemas because there is no sovereignty without the ability to leave; create the demand for alternatives before the failure, put the money where the market is still genesis, small models for every language and culture and agents with the least agency, regulate what settled, and treat constraints as the input, with Europe's values and its people on the journey.

nodes.label: Do not enter the capital race
nodes.summary: Frontier models, GPUs and data centres sit in commodity with a lead that cannot be bought back; for a small country it is the wrong end of the map.

nodes.label: The opportunity is the plumbing
nodes.summary: What stops a talented person selling to the world is company formation, cross-border hiring, payments, language, contracts and tax, each custom built today.

nodes.label: A talented person at the top of the map
nodes.summary: Anchor the map on a developer, designer, librarian or product team in a small country selling a service to a buyer abroad who would rather buy than build.

nodes.label: Fewer than one in ten firms sells across EU borders online
nodes.summary: Eurostat for 2021: 18.5% of EU enterprises sold online at home, 8.1% to other EU countries, 4.6% to the rest of the world.

nodes.label: Infrastructure is the state's job because it enables everyone
nodes.summary: The shop on the road did not pay for the road; the plumbing for selling services abroad is a road in the same sense, pooled money built once for all.

nodes.label: Estonia built the road
nodes.summary: E-Residency: 142,000 e-residents and 43,000 companies, over 4,200 founded in 2026 by mid-September; X-Road, open source under MIT, shared with Finland and Iceland.

nodes.label: No sovereignty without open source and open schemas
nodes.summary: Sovereignty means being able to leave; a road with a toll gate owned by one company is lock-in, not infrastructure.

nodes.label: What the state pays for belongs to the commons
nodes.summary: Software bought with taxes should be visible and runnable by the public, which is also how a local industry grows around it.

nodes.label: Create the demand before the day you need it
nodes.summary: Parallel services, local alternatives with fewer features, procurement that prefers data and service mobility, so a market exists before the single point of failure fails; the failures are under-documented, so the fragility is worse than the public cases show.

nodes.label: Smaller models, more of them
nodes.summary: Most work needs a model good enough for one job in one language with one culture; frontier models are for the frontier and are too expensive and too powerful for production.

nodes.label: Amalia, a public model as a public road
nodes.summary: Portugal's open model of 1 July 2026, built by universities with 5.5 million euros of EU funds, published with dataset and code as a base for others.

nodes.label: Agents with the least agency
nodes.summary: Use the model once to build the tool and run production as plain code under a behaviour policy; trust comes from less agency, not more.

nodes.label: Constraints are the input
nodes.summary: DeepSeek trained V3 in 2.788 million GPU hours on export-restricted H800 chips with custom communication code; the constraint produced the innovation.

nodes.label: A distributed workforce works when the infrastructure comes first
nodes.summary: Millions spent on Upwork as a CISO and CTO delivered faster and better because project management, structure and onboarding were built first; the right talent at a fair local price, and jobs that stay where people want to live.

nodes.label: The judo playbook in five moves
nodes.summary: Map the attrition, commoditise the plumbing, create the demand, put money where the market is genesis, regulate what settled, then map again.

nodes.label: The embassy facilitates
nodes.summary: The Ambassador role in SGraph Send was written the way an embassy works: represent, build relationships, create the conditions for growth, never hard sales.

quotes.text: A road with a toll gate owned by one company is not infrastructure; it is lock-in with tarmac.
quotes.why: Why the plumbing has to be open source and on open schemas to count as sovereignty.

quotes.text: The talent, the energy and the hunger are not the constraint.

figures.caption: A talented person in Portugal, Romania or Estonia selling a service to the world, as a Wardley map. The capital race on the right is a commodity; the red dots are the plumbing that is still custom built in most of Europe and that a state can move right; the green dots are where the market is still genesis and where the money should go.

The judo playbook in five moves: map the attrition, commoditise the plumbing, create the demand, put the money where the market is still genesis, regulate what settled, then map again. Three examples underneath of a constraint, a small state and a public model doing it.
